title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
slides: Why is Anthropic automating its own AI development?
A new report details internal automated AI research systems.
Researchers worry oversight may not keep pace with the speed.
Teams using AI-built models must audit what they cannot see.
Ask your vendor: who reviews the code AI wrote?
thread_text:
1. Anthropic automates its own R&D

A new report details internal automated AI research systems that can design, test, and improve new models. The company building the AI is now using AI to build the next AI.

2. Speed without brakes

Researchers warn oversight may not keep pace with automated research cycles that run faster than any human review process. The question is who catches mistakes when the system moves at machine speed.

3. The audit gap

Teams deploying AI-built models must audit what they cannot see: the code paths, training choices, and fixes the automation made along the way. If you cannot inspect it, you cannot trust it.

4. Vendors under pressure

Buyers are starting to ask who reviews the code AI wrote inside the models they purchase. Procurement teams now need answers on human sign-off before signing contracts.

5. Ask your vendor today

Ask your vendor one question: who reviews the code AI wrote? If they cannot name a person and a process, you have your answer.
